newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COCOA ENDS DOWN BUT NEAR HIGHS ON WEAK STG.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COCOA ENDS DOWN BUT NEAR HIGHS ON WEAK STG.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa fell in tight early trade but closed near the day's highs after a new slump by sterling sparked some industry buying, traders said.
Volume was low at 2,992 lots and traders said at least 400-500 of these were cross trades and AAs. March led with 1,128 lots, followed by December with 643.
"Volume is small. The market is quiet, waiting for more information about crops and a more definite forecast on West Africa," a trader said.
Active March opened 10 stg down at 1,075 but ended seven down after trading between 1,080 and 1,074. September was nine stg down at 1,026 and December was 10 stg lower at 1,055.
The market opened lower after New York's overnight fall but recovered some ground in afternoon trading.
"It fell this morning because New York was down overnight. It has recovered from lows because the industry is doing a bit of buying and the pound weakened again," a trader said.
However, Hamburg traders said the fall in sterling was still insufficient to tempt German buyers.
German chocolate manufacturers were continuing to delay bean and butter purchases because sterling-related savings were being offset by relatively high cocoa prices, traders said.
"Buyers enquired for first quarter beans this morning but found the 3.05 marks/kg on offer was some 0.15 pfennigs above their ideas," one trader said.
